#6148. 26 Dreamy Caribbean Hotels to Escape to This Winter

Nowhere evokes the images of white sand, turquoise water, and warm hospitality quite like the Caribbean. There are over 7,000 islands in the region, and the best Caribbean hotels can be found on just a small clutch of them. This is the ultimate place to vacation. The sunsets seem to stretch for hours and are best enjoyed with bare feet, salty sea hair, and a rum punch in hand. When it comes to choosing where to visit, it's hard to go wrong, but each spot has its own unique charm, quirks, and list of beautiful places to stay. Whether you're looking for a luxury resort with glossy interiors in the Bahamas or a boutique bolthole run by a local family in Barbados, there's an address for you on the list below. Consider this your definitive guide to the best hotels in the Caribbean.

Descending a steep hillside into a 100-acre estate is a momentous entrance anywhere, let alone one stretched out between the iconic peaks of Petit and Gros Piton, after a winding journey up and up and up the mountainside. It’s worth the climb. In bouncy Soufrière, Sugar Beach's 130 bright white villas gleam between the thick foliage and fan out over the hillsides until they reach St. Lucia’s prettiest white-sand beach. Between the chocolate, the cocktails, the sunsets, and the salt in your hair, a stay here is a full sensory experience, which continues in the evenings as the whistling frogs' calls ring out into the balmy night, echoing across the mountaintops. —Charley Ward

This namesake hillside resort set above Toiny Bay gives “wild” an unexpected new meaning when it comes to sceney St. Barts. On the scrubby southeastern point of the island, this unfussy haven is where an in-the-know social set heads to find serenity, whether via an early morning surf lesson or at the wave-lapped beach club. Rugged shoreline views and cacti-dotted greenery imbue a sense of calm from the second you’re greeted with a glass of Champagne at check-in.

Secluded infinity-pool decks boast far-flung views of the azure sea and surfers paddling out to the white caps consistently churning up on this side of the island. The suites and villas here were redesigned in 2024 by Osborn Interiors to swap in more modern touches. If St. Barts’s reputation for heaving parties and see-and-be-seen celebrities might have you thinking the Champagne-drenched French Caribbean island isn’t for you, Le Toiny probably is—and anyone else who wants the serenity of a wild coastline at their fingertips. —Shannon McMahon

This resort is a true slice of paradise, and the kind of place you'll be itching to return to the moment you leave. Expect utter peacefulness, relaxing accommodations, excellent food, and water activities galore. The spacious, contemporary cottages—30, in all—were recently redesigned to be brighter and airier, swapping out dark wood for light and granting unobstructed ocean views via large sliding glass doors. The decks are nearly as large as the bedrooms, with lounge chairs, daybeds, and private plunge pools to dip into. For those up on the hill, staff is on standby to ferry guests up and down in golf carts. As an all-inclusive property, your meals, afternoon snacks, and fresh sushi are covered, as are cocktails and beverages, like the juice of the day served at breakfast. You're here to rest and delight in the calm waters of the cove—swim, snorkel, paddleboard, or head out on a sunset cruise or deep-sea fishing trip aboard one of the property's three boats. —Madison Flager

There’s an irresistible sweetness to the rainbow skies, lush palms, and bone-white Moorish architecture of Cap Juluca, a premier luxury experience unrivaled in the Caribbean, as expected from an LVMH brand. Go for an enchanting, Caribbean-spirited, never-lift-a-finger luxury experience of textbook island bliss. Lose yourself in the tranquility and contentment of the Guerlain spa, eat at some of the premier dining spots on Anguilla, and find out how beautiful life can be at the bottom of a rum punch before being lulled into a deep sleep by the spellbinding sound of lapping waves off a humid ocean breeze—from the inside of your own villa, of course. It's an experience so good, your palate for a luxury vacation will have a new standard. —Bridget Knowles

On a hilltop overlooking turquoise Castle Harbour, Rosewood is the epitome of extravagance, from its whitewashed marble corridors right down to its powdery beach. When this swank resort first opened as Rosewood Tucker’s Point in 2009, it ushered in a new level of luxury in Bermuda. Nearly 10 years later, the bar was raised yet again with a $25 million renovation of the guest rooms and public spaces. It's now got a handsome look, a handful of additions, and a bevy of resort-wide upgrades. Expect all the bells and whistles of a full-service luxury stay: A Robert Rulewich–designed, championship-caliber golf course; several swimming pools (some adults-only, others just for kids); a state-of-the-art fitness center; a full-service Sense Spa; tennis courts; a kids club; and a private beach that will keep you drooling for days. —David LaHuta

Anguilla is a small-but-mighty island packed with luxury properties, dining options, and outstanding beaches. Barnes Bay and Meads Bay surround the Four Seasons on both sides, with waters that are occasionally rough but known to be swimmable at other times of the year. Regardless of the conditions, white beach chairs line the sand in pristine formations each morning, and three large pool areas—two kid-friendly, one adults-only—provide plenty of swimming options when the ocean is unavailable. The property stretches across the shore, which means each room provides a unique view of some combination of beachfront, ocean, palm trees, or garden. In my oceanview one-bedroom suite, we overlooked the modernist pool deck as well as the distant ocean, with a plunge pool on the balcony and ample outdoor space for afternoon lounging. The bathroom was equipped with two sinks, a large tub, and a marble walk-in shower. —Emily Adler

In a hidden corner of St. Barts, down a steep and winding road, you come to a Gauguin-like canopy of lush green vegetation, beyond which the half-moon sandy perfection of Flamands Beach reveals itself and the Cheval Blanc reigns supreme. Low-built and quietly sprawling, the property was elegantly renovated following Hurricane Irma by Parisian design supremo Jacques Grange, whose interiors speak to a chic European aesthetic of quiet indulgences. The atmosphere is almost Parisian (there’s a Guerlain spa on the premises) but with a devil-may-care attitude.

Young French culinary star Jean Imbert’s Creole-inspired menu at La Case is light but gastronomic, and the cocktails are sublime. I spent my lunches with feet in the sand at the La Cabane beach restaurant, watching a parade of Birkin bag–carrying ladies power-walking along the beach, moguls on their phones doing business, and boho French girls running into the waves in tiny Eres bikinis. It reminded me of St. Tropez’s Plage Pampelonne, but a lot less frenetic, and with an ambience that’s both relaxed and indulgent. My assigned butler would WhatsApp me when my room was done, or a spa appointment was due. But it was my private yoga sessions in the garden’s pagoda that I won’t forget in a hurry. —Vassi Chamberlain

Book a stay to experience Six Senses’s hallmark approach to barefoot luxury and a warm, welcoming vibe that befits the Spice Isle and its people. The hotel’s 71 rooms, suites, and villas are built into the slopes around the lagoon and across a bluff. In the thatched beachfront suites, each room (including the bathroom) is designed to offer direct access to a private pool and the ocean shore. Grenada is ever so tiny—12 miles by 21 miles long. Still, the resort is set away from the bustle of Grenada’s capital, St. George's, the popular beaches of Grand Anse and BBC, and treks into the rainforests—getting to any of these takes about 30 minutes by car. Out of 200 employees here, 180 have been hired locally—in many cases, hyper-locally, from the parish of St. David. This is part of the Six Senses commitment to integrate with local communities across its global footprint. The result is a resort that mimics the friendliness and easy hospitality of Grenada’s people, and the best way to enjoy this is to slip right into an island state of mind with them. —Arati Menon

Travelers who want to feel like they’re summering at a friend’s beachfront estate will thoroughly appreciate the laid-back vibe of the Potlatch Club on the isle of Eleuthera. The lush property has only 11 keys on 12 acres, a seamless service team that's worked together for more than 20 years at other hotels, and a cluster of storied structures, some of which date back to 1923. In the 1950s, after the property was purchased by a trio of socialites, it became a private hideaway for celebrities like Paul McCartney, who honeymooned here with his late wife Linda in 1969.

Current owners Bruce Loshusan and his business partner Hans Febles began work on the resort in 2016; Loshusan recruited Nassau-based interior designer Amanda Lindroth to help produce the dreamy, relaxed atmosphere that encompasses what people find enchanting about island life: white shiplap ceilings, pink coral stone floors that extend to the bathrooms, and cozy wooden porches with rattan daybeds and chairs. —Alexandra Sanidad

From the moment the resort’s yacht glides into the serene waters of Yacht Harbor in Sprat Bay, the transition from passenger to prized guest is practically instantaneous. Peter Island is the largest private island in the British Virgin Islands, yet the resort has managed to capture an utterly intimate vibe. The resort strives to be as sustainable as possible; it has a reverse osmosis water purification plant and two wind turbines that can generate up to 75% of the island's power. And yet Peter Island still doesn't mess with what works, and leans into a familial flavor of hospitality that feels like you’re at your favorite aunt and uncle’s for the holidays. —Kat Chen

Images of Rockhouse’s thatch-roof stone villas and bright red ladders dropping into the sea have come to represent a certain brand of Jamaican cool. The property, currently celebrating its 50th anniversary, isn’t shy about honoring its place in pop culture history: Bob Marley and the Rolling Stones once jumped off its iconic cliffs, and reggae and dancehall ephemera line the walls. Rooms are simple but still retain an essence of the sleepy 1970s Negril that originally defined the property: Four-poster beds are draped with mosquito nets and decorated with locally sourced quilts; in the villa rooms, palm-fringed outdoor showers mean morning routines are accompanied by birdsong; and the cool, simple stone floors keep you feeling in tune with island life. Meanwhile, food here is a primer in Jamaican classics, especially at jerk spot Pushcart, where DJs take over the sound systems for regular dance parties. The Rockhouse crowd knows how to have a good time. —Lale Arikoglu

Cap Cana is chock-full of resorts to get away from it all, but tastemakers, design lovers, and those looking to instill envy in their followers will want to head straight to St. Regis’s first foray into the Dominican Republic. While you can expect the same high-end amenities of the brand—butlers on call to arrange excursions, seafood towers, Champagne, a luxe spa—what sets this hotel apart are the details grounded in Dominican culture. Set on 16 acres of beachfront property, the rambling, indoor-outdoor resort with 200 rooms, including 36 suites, features tropical plants, patterned brickwork, and curved ceilings adorned with wickerwork. Artworks by Dominican artists are peppered throughout the building, lending a gallery-like vibe.

As for local flavors, dine at Cassava for breakfast, lunch, or dinner, and head to the Amber Room for a cigar and two fingers of rum. In between, you can play at the Jack Nicklaus Signature Punta Espada golf course, which abuts the property; indulge in services at the salon and the spa; or just unwind on the beach or by the pool (try to score one of the private cabanas). Whatever you decide, as you languorously wander from bed to breakfast, from beach to pool, from lunch to cocktails to dinner, you can relax knowing that everything will be taken care of. —Damian Fallon

You can become a little numb to beauty in St. Barts, but even after having been on the island for days, I think I squealed when I pulled into Eden Rock. It’s just so perfect—so chic, so glamorous, but in this easy, island-appropriate way. It’s the type of place that just being there makes you feel like the most glam, sun-kissed version of yourself. The hotel is almost entirely surrounded by calm, gin-bottle- blue water that’s heavenly for a swim. There’s a diving platform a little ways out; you can take out rafts and paddle around the point, and there’s a reef if you want to snorkel. The rooms are lovely and elegant, with a subtle Carib-meets-nautical vibe, at once bright and airy.

When it comes to the food, rockstar chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten is in charge of the menu at the main restaurant, and the resort’s breakfast spread is wild in scope and quality; don’t miss it. Sure, you could have a delightful breakfast by your private pool, but the people-watching here is too good—you’d be missing an opportunity if you stayed in. It’s a pretty diverse crowd in some ways, but the common denominator, to tell it straight, is money. This place is not cheap, but it’s one of the rare hotels that is absolutely worth it. The setting is unparalleled, and the food, service, and design are top of the top. There is no way you’ll go and not dream (maybe nightly) about going back—it’s that special. —Rebecca Misner

As COMO’s sole property in the Americas, Parrot Cay's renowned luxury experience makes it an unrivaled property in Turks and Caicos. The pinnacle of bespoke solitude, it's located on a private island enmeshed in the wilderness. You arrive after a 15-minute chauffeured drive from Providenciales International Airport, then a 20-minute panoramic boat ride through cays and turquoise waves hugged by mangroves. It’s primeval in nature and worlds away, despite its ease of access from the main island. The private, white-sand beach—with miles of clear-water sandbars inviting you to walk across, float around, and laze about for ages—is the main reason why the property has been dubbed by locals as "the Maldives of the Americas," despite being entirely singular in the impression it makes. If you’re seeking a romantic getaway inspired by an itch for an immersive nature escape, this is the place to go—and I recommend booking a private beach house with your own plunge pool for the full, immersive experience. —B.K.

Step onto the grounds of Coral Reef Club, and you would be forgiven for feeling like you’ve been transported back 50 years to a bygone era of old-school glamour. Families frolic by the ocean on chic sun loungers, while glamorous older couples are served sherries by attentive waiters in immaculately pressed uniforms. The 88 suites and cottages with plunge pools or wraparound balconies are intertwined among 12 acres of lush gardens, rooms merging classic Bajan style (think colorful art and cane furnishings) with English touches such as pretty verandas with wooden railings and old-fashioned outdoor lampshades.

Breakfast is an elaborate affair with both a large buffet offering everything from Bajan fish cakes to fresh pancakes and a made-to-order menu. Those with space left over for lunch can enjoy anything from local roti to juicy Cajun shrimp tacos over views of the crashing waves. But dinner is where it really gets glamorous, where stone pillars and the most attentive waiters you may ever come across serve a classic European menu infused with Caribbean touches to the sounds of a live singer. –Jessica Rach

Though it's just 21 miles long, Grenada packs a punch: You will find lush rainforests, nature reserves, spice plantations, the charming town of St. George’s, and beaches so perfect that they look photoshopped. For those seeking a serene island escape, the 28-room Silversands Beach House is the place. Time seems to stop here, a feeling that begins the moment you drive up the entrance and the turquoise waters of Portici Beach come into view.

The rooms and suites are so lovely—private terraces, floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the sea, calming shades of cream and light wood—that you may never want to leave; but the dreamy infinity pool and sandy beach just a few steps away make a great case for venturing out. The food at the upscale Mediterranean-inspired Azzurro restaurant is another highlight: Pasta is made in-house, seafood is locally sourced, and the roasted vegetable pizza is the perfect finale to a day spent on the water. There’s also plenty to experience nearby, and the staff will gladly guide you through activities, whether it’s touring the beautiful island or a rum tasting. The vibes are unhurried, gracious, and sweet, and you’ll feel yourself slipping into island time along with everyone else. —Pallavi Kumar

There are Caribbean beach resorts, and then there is Little Dix Bay, which was completely rebuilt after being decimated by hurricanes in 2017, celebrating its 60th anniversary in 2024. It’s undoubtedly got the bells and whistles—a truly transcendent spa, one of the best rum collections in the Caribbean, and so forth—but what sets Little Dix Bay apart is its staff, some of whom have worked here for over 30 years.

There are 42 guestrooms, 35 suites, two beach houses, and two hillside villas with a contemporary-yet-textured aesthetic. With sleek furniture juxtaposed against stone walls (a reference to the island’s iconic boulders), a minibar station that feels homey and not like an afterthought, and comfortable beds perfect for pressing snooze on your alarm clock, there isn’t a bad room in the house here. It’s the kind of place where guests at checkout will turn to their butler and ask, “Same time next year?” —Todd Plummer

It’s easy to imagine that very little has changed at this 1950s-era resort since John F. Kennedy absconded to Cottage 25 to chip away at his inaugural address and Oscar Hammerstein wrote The Sound of Music while taking in the killer ocean views. The green-striped awnings shading vast terraces and the interiors’ cream-colored paneling offset by dark wood, along with the tea and sandwiches served at four sharp every afternoon, enhance that caught-in-time feeling. That Ralph Lauren has had a major hand in the design in recent years is a delightful non-surprise, with playful preppiness on display at every turn, like the bar with its deep booth benches upholstered in navy-and-white stripes and photos of bygone guests, like Warren Beatty, covering the walls. —Charlie Hobbs

Built in 1970 and family-run ever since, The Sandpiper’s original charm remains, and despite being renovated (the suites are particularly modern), a thread of tradition runs through this property and nods to its history. Fifty rooms—some with their own plunge pools—span two-story, pavilion-style houses surrounded by lush vegetation. Four contemporary suites with direct beach access and ocean views sit separately in the hotel’s tropical gardens and offer modern comforts like a complimentary bar, White Company amenities, and even a personally appointed butler.

As one of the world’s most desirable winter destinations, the Caribbean has an abundance of resort options based on a familiar model. These are the expansive beachfront properties with grand entries, cavernous lobbies, and ostentatious styling featuring a plethora of palm trees, pools, and piña coladas. I’m not suggesting this can’t make for a fantastic getaway—but if this is what you desire, Rock House is not for you. Located in tropical Turks and Caicos but taking its inspiration from the Mediterranean, Rock House offers guests something refreshingly different.

Opened in 2022 as an addition to the renowned Grace Bay Resorts brand, Rock House synthesizes 30 years of luxury resort expertise into a modern European-style experience that satisfies the senses and nourishes the soul. Every detail, from the painstaking dedication to preserving the native ecology surrounding it to the in-house phone app that enables you to effortlessly communicate with the guest experience team without leaving the beach or your private infinity pool, has been thoughtfully considered. Families are welcome, but Rock House may appeal most to lovers and those seeking a truly tranquil environment to relax and recharge. —Caryn B. Davis

Bermuda is generally divided into two parts, east and west, with the capital of Hamilton somewhat in the middle. Most luxury resorts reside in Hamilton or on the east end, but one historic hotel is found on the quieter west end. The resort’s iconic pink cottages, four bars and restaurants, two-tiered pool, and expansive grounds that include four private beaches have been brought into the 21st century after a refresh—no small feat since some architectural details date back to the 1600s.

The 86 cottages are chic, with a tropical-inspired color palette, dark wood statement beds, quirky rattan chairs, and boldly patterned textiles. Vintage-inspired pastel-colored scalloped umbrellas and cushy lounge chairs populate the refurbished pool area and its accompanying bar and restaurant, which also sports a magnificently detailed shell-encrusted back bar. A highlight is the Sunken Harbor Club (an outpost of the same-named Brooklyn bar), which is decorated with shipwreck treasures rescued by the late Bermudian diving legend Teddy Tucker. Bermudian-rooted cuisine is on offer, with dishes like miso-marinated black cod complementing classic island cocktails and new creations by barmaster St. John Frizell. —Devorah Lev-Tov

Combining sustainability best practices with true luxury, this sleek eco-resort is a model for Dominica and the wider Caribbean, demonstrating that you needn’t sacrifice creature comforts to have a green vacation. Coulibri Ridge was built with environmental consciousness at its core—a construction process that took the Canadian-Dominican owners a whopping 15 years to complete. Now, what was once a colonial-era citrus plantation has been transformed into a hillside retreat that aims to be self-sufficient. The 285-acre property is completely powered by the sun via 225 solar panels and 288 recyclable non-lithium batteries; two communal pools are solar-heated and kept clean not with chlorine, but by using a copper ionizer. But if you think the resort is more functional than fancy, think again. Guests are treated to modern studios, lofts, and penthouses with sweeping views of the water, tropical and bountiful breakfasts (included in the rate), and a spa with open-air treatment rooms. —C.D.

This family-owned boutique hotel’s trump card, besides the photogenic striped pink scalloped umbrellas, is its quarter-mile of powder-soft beach in a sleepy cove. Pastel-hued suites are dotted around tropical gardens festooned with palms and banana leaves and a terra-cotta pool terrace, which feels suspended over views of the bay. Tastefully dressed in subdued fabric of hand-printed corals, whitewashed rattan, and bamboo, rooms spill onto terraces framed by bougainvillea, inhaling the salty breeze. The main spaces read like a British country estate, with a drawing room and cavernous hall, just with exotic pinks and greens and plantation shutters—a blend that reflects the island's rich (and often checkered) history.

Mornings at Cobblers Cove recall country clubs of yore, where a genteel breakfast is occasionally interrupted by the pop of a tennis serve or a Champagne cork. Afternoons typically slump between lounge chairs and the balmy sea, where guests can paddle out in search of turtles or gently part the calm, glassy water on a paddleboard. When not leaning into the hotel’s afternoon tea tradition or its phenomenal spa, sailing and water skiing sessions take place every day, and guests can join local fishermen on “catch of the day” adventures. The on-site restaurant preserves its status as one of the island’s top eateries, while weekly buffets and barbecues show off local dishes in a more buttoned-down setting. —Rosalyn Wikeley

Far from the tourist hustle and bustle of the northwestern coast, Jamaica’s chicest and arguably most famous address is located on the northeastern coastline of Oracabessa—a jewel of about 5,000 people, with a thriving community of creatives. Writer Ian Fleming became so enamoured with Oracabessa while on assignment with the British Navy during World War II that he returned to buy a property, building GoldenEye, where he would go on to write all 13 James Bond novels during his winter stays. In 1976, Bob Marley became the owner, later selling it to Chris Blackwell—founder of Island Records, who expanded the property to include a range of private huts, cottages, and villas dotted around the tropical 40-acre grounds. The beachside hideaway is home to four restaurants and bars, including the laid-back bamboo bar which serves Jamaican jerk barbecue right on the sandy Low Cay beachfront. —Ruth C. White

Colorful is the best adjective for Jumby Bay. Emerald-green lizards dart up whitewashed walls, iridescent hummingbirds hover over pink Mexican creepers, and yellow-chested bananaquits search for crumbs on breakfast tables. There are blindingly white sands to cross and turquoise waters to slip into for a world of plump orange starfish, yellow-tailed snappers, and blue tang. Beneath all this shifting color is the lush, 300-acre private island that remains one of the most exclusive in the Caribbean. Its “no cars, no keys” policy brings a feeling of intimacy to the three restaurants, spa, 40 rooms and suites, and 14 villas that make up the hotel, all of which offer luxury as dazzling as the island’s colors.

The generously sized suites come with a little entrance courtyard where wicker chairs swing in the warm breeze. Terraces overlook the sea or are inset with a pool. Some bathrooms spill outside with vast tubs waiting under palm fronds. Step outside your room to enjoy Taittinger on tap (part of the inclusive rates, which also offer limitless water sports) or sip daiquiris made with local black pineapple. Food served at the Estate House, once part of the original sugar plantation, brims with a sense of place. But the best experience has to be a rum tasting with the barman, which leads to serious Caribbean contentment. A stand-out amenity: access to The Hut, the hotel's private island beach club. —Mary Lussiana

How we choose the best hotels in the Caribbean

Every hotel review on this list has been written by a Condé Nast Traveler journalist who knows the destination and has visited that property. When choosing hotels, our editors consider properties across price points that offer an authentic and insider experience of a destination, keeping design, location, service, and sustainability credentials top of mind.

This article was originally published on Condé Nast Traveller UK. It has been updated with new information since its original publish date.

As the most discerning, up-to-the-minute voice in all things travel, Condé Nast Traveler is the global citizen’s bible and muse, offering both inspiration and vital intel. We understand that time is the greatest luxury, which is why Condé Nast Traveler mines its network of experts and influencers so that you never waste a meal, a drink, or a hotel stay wherever you are in the world.

#6147. Democrats mulling Iran war funding cutoff strategy

Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., talks with reporters in the Capitol on Sept. 30. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call)

A group of prominent Senate Democrats is pushing to use a must-pass spending bill to cut off funding for the Iran war, complicating the path toward a bipartisan deal for averting a partial government shutdown next month.

Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., said Thursday he is working on legislative language ending the war that he wants attached to the next continuing resolution that is needed by Dec. 11, when current funding runs out.

“I know it’s going to be my main push,” he said. “I have to work with colleagues to try to find some language that works. And I’m not there yet, but I’ve told everybody that’s an opportunity.”

Democratic Sens. Michael Bennet of Colorado, Chris Van Hollen of Maryland, Tammy Duckworth of Illinois and independent Bernie Sanders of Vermont released a statement Thursday that they would oppose any deal that does not include “language that restricts the Trump Administration from using appropriated funds to continue his war against Iran.”

“When we vote on appropriations, we intend to fund the government and stop funds for this war,” the senators said. “It is what the American people demand, and what they deserve.”

It is unlikely that Republicans, who are in control of both chambers of Congress until January, not to mention the Oval Office beyond that, would agree to such a deal.

House Appropriations Chairman Tom Cole, R-Okla., said earlier this week that “a Republican Congress is not going to send bills to a Republican president that he's going to veto.”

While ending the war is a top priority of Democrats as they take back power in the new Congress, insisting on doing so this year could lead to a Christmas-time partial government shutdown. If a shutdown starts after Dec. 11, it’s possible it would still be ongoing when Democrats take control of both chambers in January.

But some Democrats appeared to still be weighing how quickly to push for a cutoff of war funding.

Senate Appropriations ranking member Patty Murray, D-Wash, said that whether or not Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth remains in his job, “we’re still going to have language stopping this war.”

She was coy on whether that fight would take place on the anticipated continuing resolution in December or wait until next year when Democrats take back power, saying that lawmakers are “looking at all options.”

Democrats are committed to ending the "reckless and costly war of choice in Iran," House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., said Thursday. He deferred to House Appropriations ranking member Rosa DeLauro, D-Conn., "to see what’s possible in advance of Dec. 11" in talks with the other top appropriators.

"I don’t want to get out ahead of Congresswoman DeLauro, but House Democrats have uniformly opposed providing any additional money to Donald Trump’s war machine. to Pete Hegseth’s war machine, over in the Middle East," Jeffries said.

It’s not clear how long a potential continuing resolution would last, and DeLauro said earlier this week that she wants it to be as short as possible.

The Office of Management and Budget has not yet submitted “anomalies” — changes to the current spending levels to be included in the continuing resolution — to Congress.

The administration is considering options including a stopgap bill that would run through March, sources familiar with the talks said. But no decision on the timing covered by the anomalies has been made.

Aris Folley, Jacob Fulton and Michael Macagnone contributed to this report.

#6146. Where to go in 2027

Learn how to get started earning and redeeming rewards so you can make the most of your everyday spending.

See how far your points, miles and dollars go in TPG's first loyalty report.

See how TPG ranks the top US airlines for 2026.

Curated annually by TPG’s team of travel experts, this year’s Where to Go list highlights particularly exciting moments happening across the globe in 2027, including hotly anticipated and fabulous new hotels, milestone museum openings, travel-worthy celestial events, new UNESCO designations, new flight routes, major sporting events and so much more. And for 2027, we’ve pulled out all the stops: Below, you can explore our new interactive map displaying the 22 destinations that earned a spot on our list.

Now more than ever, exploring new and familiar destinations fosters curiosity, connectedness, and, perhaps most importantly, compassion. It’s time to put those hard-earned points and miles toward your dream trip — and we’ve got just the ticket.

Epic celestial events and ancient landmarks with no galaxy far, far away required.

Caribbean luxury that rewards every dollar you spend.

Best in July through August + December through March

New sightseeing trains and upscale points hotels make Japan’s stunning northern island even more alluring in 2027.

For those who want to experience Hokkaido’s beautiful countryside by train, Hokkaido Railway Company will debut two scenic tourist trains in 2027: the Red Star luxury train in February, when the region is blanketed in Hokkaido’s signature fluffy snow, and the Blue Star premium class train in June, just in time for Hokkaido’s lavender season.

And for skiers and snowboarders who are looking to experience Hokkaido’s incredible winter sports scene, Moxy Niseko will debut in late 2026, just in time for the start of ski season. Other exciting Niseko openings to look forward to in the coming years include Six Senses Niseko and an Aman property. In nearby Sapporo, new and forthcoming points hotels are plentiful, too: 2025 saw the opening of the InterContinental Sapporo, and both Hyatt Centric and Fairmont are planned for 2027 into 2028. -⁠Ellie Nan Storck

World-class dining and hotels to help fans refuel between Women’s World Cup matches.

One of the most accessible host cities of the Women’s World Cup is also among the most captivating. Beyond the pitch, visitors can experience the city’s dining renaissance, the long-awaited Museum of Image and Sound and the one of the oldest national history museums in the Americas, recently reopened after a 2018 fire. Plus, Rio (and nearby Maricá) is the midst of a luxury hotel boom, with exciting points properties opening over the coming years. December will bring the opening of Accor’s Sofitel Rio de Janeiro Ipanema, and over the next few years, Marriott will debut an eco-luxe Ritz Carlton Reserve and an all-inclusive JW Marriott in Maricá. -⁠Rachel Craft

Best in March through May + October through November

A perennial favorite is experiencing a luxury hotel boom.

Mexico’s massive capital never lacked excellent hotel options, but a recent slate of renovations and openings has us more excited than ever to revisit the city. The St. Regis Mexico City completed a multimillion dollar renovation with Frida Kahlo-inspired design elements in Sept. 2026. Hyatt loyalists can look forward to the February opening of the colorful new Standard Hotel in the Tabacalera neighborhood, followed by the April debut of the luxe Park Hyatt in Polanco. Other upcoming projects to look forward to include a Mama Shelter (part of the ALL Accor hotel loyalty program) in the heart of Roma Norte, set to open by the end of 2026, as well as Pendry Mexico City and Rosewood Mexico City, both planned for 2027. -⁠Lyndsey Matthews

The perfect mix of new luxury hotels, a distinct wine scene and endless opportunities to get outside.

In the Texas Hill Country, charming towns steeped in German culture are surrounded by award-winning wineries, idyllic swimming holes and Main Streets packed with restaurants, shops and some of the friendliest people in the Lone Star State. Near Fredericksburg, the epicenter of the Hill Country’s must-visit charm, Waldorf Astoria is opening its first Texas property, while Aman has plans for a secluded ranch retreat of its own. Add mouthwatering barbecue, legendary live music, popular rivers to float and an expanding Austin-Bergstrom International Airport (AUS), and there are more reasons than ever to head for the hills. -⁠Tanner Saunders

Rich in natural beauty, this coastal California town is ready to step into the spotlight.

Wellness travelers, adventure travelers and everyone in between will fall for this sleepy coastal enclave along the northern California coast. Unwind at Marriott Bonvoy’s newest adventure lodge after exploring the recently opened Great Redwood Trail or sampling the latest additions to the town’s renowned sustainable food and wine scene. And thanks to nonstop flights from Alaska Airlines and Southwest and $20 million in roadwork funding, Mendocino is easier than ever to reach. -⁠Rachel Craft

Experience a quieter side of India in one of the world’s lushest biodiversity hotspots

Like many of the best places, it can take a lot of time and effort to get to Coorg, a hill station in India’s verdant, biodiverse Western Ghats. But it is well worth it to see this little-visited region rife with endemic wildlife including elephants, leopards and myriad avian species. Spend your days sampling world-class coffee at the area’s many plantations, hiking the misty mountain trails and recentering yourself with immersive multiday Ayurvedic wellness programs at the stunning new Leela Coorg Forest Sanctuary. -⁠Eric Rosen

In anticipation of hosting the EXPO 2027, the Serbian capital is undergoing a major glow-up

From May 15 to Aug.15, the Serbian capital will host a specialized world exposition with 140-plus countries gathering to showcase innovations in architecture and design. In anticipation of the event, Belgrade is debuting several major projects of its own, including a Nikola Tesla Museum designed by Zaha Hadid Architects. The former main railway station will become the new permanent home of the Historical Museum of Serbia, while the Museum of the City of Belgrade and the Museum of Natural History Belgrade will also open in new facilities. Finally, the Aeronautical Museum of Belgrade will also complete a modernization project in 2027. To accommodate the influx of visitors, the city already opened a St. Regis in 2024, while the InterContinental Belgrade is accepting reservations from next March, with a Ritz-Carlton also anticipated to open, too. -⁠Lyndsey Matthews

Best in May through June, September through October

A pair of new destination-worthy hotels, both bookable with points.

Hyatt and Marriott will both debut luxury properties in Detroit come 2027. Hilton’s new hotel, the NoMad Detroit, will open inside the historic Michigan Grand Central Station, a once-abandoned Beaux-Arts landmark restored by Ford. Later in the year, the Marriott Edition will open as part of a ground-up development, bringing downtown Detroit its first five-star hotel. -⁠Carly Helfand

A new film festival is just one facet of this art-meets-outdoors jewel.

Between hosting its first Sundance Film Festival and celebrating 50 years of the iconic Pearl Street Mall, Colorado’s trendy cultural hub is going all out. Visitors can also look forward to new dining concepts from Michelin-recognized chefs, new interactive art labs and easy access to new Rocky Mountain hiking trails. An hour away, Denver International Airport (DEN) is expanding to accommodate increased traffic from United, Southwest and even Delta. -⁠Rachel Craft

Jungle-covered islands and seas teeming with marine life beckon explorers beyond the bright lights of Bali.

Cruise companies are lining up new expeditions to explore the Indonesian archipelago’s untouched corners, including a seven-day sailing aboard Uniworld’s Aqua Blu that will stop in Komodo National Park and the Spice Islands, Ponant’s team-up with Smithsonian Journeys on a 15-day jaunt around the Maluku islands among other ports of call and specialized dive-focused sailings in wild West Papua, reef-rich Raja Ampat and untamed Borneo from Swan Hellenic and Noble Caledonia. It’s the best way to experience regions of the Indonesian archipelago most folks never see. -⁠Eric Rosen

Australia’s first Michelin Guide, new luxury hotels and experiences, nonstop access from the U.S. and an extraordinary mix of world-class wine, wildlife and wilderness make 2027 South Australia’s moment on the global stage.

Australia’s first Michelin Guide and United’s nonstop San Francisco-Adelaide flight are putting South Australia within easier reach — and on the global culinary map, too. A significant transformation of Adelaide Central Market, Australia’s first Treehouse Hotel and new luxury stays are adding fresh reasons to visit, alongside the Barossa and McLaren Vale wine regions and the wildlife and rugged beauty of Kangaroo Island. -⁠Tanner Saunders

Best in April through June, September through October

Natural wonders and a burgeoning culture scene without the crowds.

Though Kazakhstan first made a name for itself as a nature travel destination, this Eurasian country wants the world to know there’s more to it than its glorious landscapes. Travelers can enjoy a new art museum and immersive ethno-village in the cultural capital of Almaty, check into new hotels in the Burabay resort region or combine natural and cultural wonders at the newly inscribed Mangystau Rock Mosques UNESCO World Heritage Site. With plans to launch the first-ever direct flight from the U.S. in 2027, this hidden gem may not stay hidden for long. -⁠Rachel Craft

Best in May through June, September through October

Two iconic cultural institutions, back and better than ever.

The Pergamon Museum will reopen in June after a multi-year renovation, debuting a fully redesigned Museum of Islamic Art and making the Pergamon Altar accessible for the first time in more than a decade. Later in the year, the Bauhaus Archive will reopen after extensive renovations with a new annex building. With nonstop options from the U.S. on United, Delta and Lufthansa — and strong Hilton and Marriott footprints downtown — early points bookings are a smart play for visiting Berlin in 2027. -⁠Carly Helfand

Best in April through June, September through November

Experience a slower type of journey that has captivated travelers for over 1,000 years.

Special events will be taking place at waystations along this ancient pilgrimage trail throughout the Holy Year of 2027. Among the highlights are braving the wine battle in Haro at the end of June, or attending St. James’s Feast Day on July 25 in Santiago de Compostela, where you can see the famous swinging of the Botafumeiro silver incense burner and attend an awe-inspiring mass in the Praza do Obradoiro. Aside from a full calendar of culinary festivals and lively concerts in Santiago, you can take in quieter stretches of the trail among the forested peaks of Cantabria and the vineyards of Rioja. -⁠Eric Rosen

Astrotourism investments and a highly anticipated points hotel transformation.

Dramatic coastal landscapes, the new Atlantic Canada UNESCO Tourism Corridor and the re-opening of the transformed The Algonquin Resort St. Andrews by-the-Sea, Autograph Collection resort make a compelling case for a 2027 visit to New Brunswick. Specifically, we’re excited to check out the Bay of Fundy Dark Sky Corridor that’s set to open in 2027 — a 137-mile stretch that could be the densest cluster of dark-sky and observatory areas on the planet. A stargazer’s dream come true. -⁠Madison Blancaflor

A burgeoning wine scene, an exciting UNESCO designation and outdoor attractions aplenty give one of BC’s prettiest regions a well deserved moment in the spotlight

With plenty of sunny days and a generally milder climate than the rest of British Columbia, the Okanagan Valley is becoming an increasingly compelling alternative to larger wine regions; oenophiles can look forward to sipping wines from smaller producers (small but mighty; there are over 200) in a community-forward and breathtaking lakeside setting.

Those in search of a city getaway should head to Kelowna, the valley’s largest metropolis set along the breezy shorelines of Okanagan Lake, where a major culinary moment is afoot. Recently designated Canada’s first UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy — a designation that honors not only the city’s agricultural innovation and culinary creativity, but the traditional foodways and land stewardship of the indigenous Syilx people — Kelowna offers a fast-growing restaurant scene (many with a sustainable, farm-to-table focus) and its own array of impressive wineries. -⁠Ellie Nan Storck

Travelers can look forward to fully restored access to Denali Park Road for the first time in six years

With more access now than ever, thanks to both recently expanded Alaska Airlines routes to nearby Fairbanks International Airport (FAI) and the very exciting full reopening of Denali Park Road for the summer season, 2027 is the year to plan an epic trip to Denali National Park. And the fun doesn’t stop there — Holland America, celebrating 80 years of Alaskan exploration, will complete a massive transformation of Holland America Denali Lodge, debuting 72 new guest rooms, updated public spaces and refreshed dining programs. Beyond the park, the Alaska Railroad — which celebrated its centennial in 2023 — is a great way travelers can experience a legendary scenic trip between Anchorage, Talkeetna, Denali and Fairbanks. -⁠Ellie Nan Storck

Expanded access from the U.S. and newly awarded Michelin key hotel recognition.

Delta is adding a new nonstop route from L.A. to Manila and Philippine Airlines is joining the oneworld alliance, making a trip to the gorgeous islands of The Philippines easier than ever in 2027. Head to the islands early in the year for milder temperatures, vibrant festivals and the chance to ethically swim with majestic whale sharks in Donsol, Sorsogon. Nature lovers and beach loungers can also enjoy luxury properties like the Raffles Makati and the forthcoming Mandarin Oriental Makati, Manila (opening in December) or use points to book the brand new AC Hotel by Marriott Manila. -⁠Madison Blancaflor

Best in June through September, January through March

These lush African islands are ready for their moment in the sun.

Thanks to its pristine tropical forests and rare wildlife species, in 2025 São Tomé and Principe became the first country in the world whose entire territory, both land and sea, was designated as a UNESCO biosphere reserve. This past year, the country scored a second UNESCO designation for its historical roças, or colonial agricultural estates, making São Tomé and Principe ripe for discovery. Even better — you can use your Star Alliance points and miles to fly direct from Lisbon on TAP and Hilton points can set you up for a beachy stay at the luxurious Sundy Praia – Principe Collection. -⁠Eric Rosen

Best in April through May, September through October

For travelers ready to venture beyond familiar South American tourism destinations and experience a different side of the continent.

Travelers who have already visited Peru, Brazil, Argentina and other South American hot spots can find something different in the continent’s less-visited interior. Don’t go expecting a long list of world-famous sights or extensive tourism infrastructure. Instead, go for a quieter, slower-paced trip shaped by Indigenous Guaraní culture and landscapes ranging from the vast Chaco lowlands to the biodiverse remnants of the Atlantic Forest along the Paraná River. New attractions are adding reasons to visit: MUVA Museo Viedma, a museum exploring Paraguay’s Guaraní-Jesuit heritage through murals by artist Manuel Viedma, opened in Misiones in May 2026, and Asunción’s Museo de Ciencias plans to open a planetarium in 2028. -⁠Mackenzie Roche

#6144. Van Hollen announces bid for majority leader, but Schumer says he has the votes

Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., left, has announced a challenge to current Senate Minority Leader Charles Schumer, D-N.Y. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo)

Sen. Chris Van Hollen announced Thursday night that he would run for Senate majority leader, launching a challenge to Sen. Charles E. Schumer of New York, the current Democratic leader.

Van Hollen, a Maryland Democrat first elected to the Senate in 2016, served in leadership in the House and has been chairman of both the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee. He has said since the midterm elections he was listening to fellow Senate Democrats about the possibility of a run for the top job.

“In this election, the American people called for change. They called for a change from Donald Trump’s disastrous policies but even bigger than that, a change from the status quo that isn’t working for working people,” Van Hollen said in a statement. “It’s now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership. This is not about any one person – it’s about answering the call of the American people. That is why I’m running for Senate Majority Leader.”

Schumer has already said he has the votes needed to continue serving as the leader.

“I welcome any discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead. I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished together — 55 seats and counting is an amazing result — and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader. I look forward to leading our new Democratic majority and delivering for the American people,” Schumer said in a statement.

Schumer's supporters were quick to highlight the success at the ballot box in 2026, with the Democratic caucus potentially growing to 56 seats if former Rep. Mary Peltola prevails in Alaska.

“Chuck has outlined an aggressive plan for the new Democratic majority which is directly responsive to the message we heard from the voters, and he has the experience and unique mastery of the Senate process to make it happen,” Sen. Angus King, a Maine independent who caucuses with the Democrats, said in a statement. “Why would you fire the manager when you just won the World Series?”

In keeping with the World Series theme, Sen. Tammy Baldwin, D-Wis., echoed King with her own statement of support for Schumer.

“The Brewers just had a record season, and next year is not the time to change our management," Baldwin said. "The same is true in the Senate.”

In an interview with MS NOW about his run, Van Hollen conceded that Schumer would be the favorite in the secret-ballot contest, which will take place in December.

“Am I the underdog? Yes,” Van Hollen said. “You’re talking about an incumbent who uses the power of incumbency to, you know, provide deals to people.”

Van Hollen outlined legislative priorities including restoring Medicaid funding that Republicans cut in last year's budget reconciliation law and extending Affordable Care Act tax credits. But he suggested Democrats need to go further.

"We need to extend tax credits for the Affordable Care Act, but we can’t stop there, right? We have a completely broken health care system. It’s become profits, not people. And so my view is, we also need in the first 100 days to make health care more affordable for tens of millions of people," Van Hollen said. "We need to immediately make it clear that nobody’s going to pay one penny to subsidize data centers. ... We need to make sure that we have a livable minimum wage."

He also said he would not take sides in contested Democratic primaries, and he would make sure the DSCC did not take money from the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, or AIPAC.

Van Hollen's early backers include progressive Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, who emerged from a hotly contested Democratic primary in Michigan while the Senate Democratic political apparatus was backing Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich.

“In April, I was the first candidate in the country to call on Senator Chris Van Hollen to lead Senate Democrats, and I am proud to stand with him in his bid to become Senate Majority Leader,” El-Sayed said in a statement. “Michiganders demand money out of politics, money in pockets, and Medicare for All. Sen. Chris Van Hollen offers both the courage to go toe-to-toe with the Trump administration to deliver for working people and the experience to maneuver the Senate caucus. It’s why he has my full support to lead our caucus.”

#6143. JSX Adds New Route From NY

JSX is launching a new nonstop route between the New York metro area and North Texas.

Starting Feb. 17, the public charter service will connect Teterboro Airport in New Jersey with Dallas Love Field. Flights will operate daily.

The service will be available only to members of the carrier’s free loyalty program, Club JSX.

“New York City and Dallas are two of America’s most influential business and cultural centers, and we believe traveling between them should be as seamless as the opportunities that connect them,” JSX CEO Alex Wilcox said in a news release. “As we continue expanding our network, our focus remains on giving customers something increasingly rare in air travel: more of their time back. With this new daily service, we’re bringing the simplicity, comfort, and convenience of JSX to one of the country’s most important travel corridors.”

JSX added service to Teterboro, which it markets as New York City, in 2025. It also serves Westchester County Airport, located just north of New York.

#6142. 11 Best Vacation Rentals in Riviera Maya for Beach Access, Private Pools, and Jungle Views

From the bustling city of Cancún to the somewhat more tranquil bohemian beach town of Tulum, the Riviera Maya is home to some of Mexico’s most idyllic beaches along the Caribbean. Featuring turquoise waters, windswept bays, and wide swaths of verdant jungle harboring hidden cenotes, this region of the Yucatán Peninsula delivers equal parts serenity and adventure. After living in Mexico for over 10 years, I’ve stayed in and driven through many of the towns and beaches that make up this region, and it's hard to choose a favorite.

As wonderful as the beachfront views, jungle tranquility, and local activities are here, the vacation rentals in the Riviera Maya are equally as impressive. They have a way of making the surrounding nature feel even more pristine. Whether you’re venturing to the region solo or traveling with friends and family, there are gorgeous options for nearly every type of traveler, each offering a personalized way to visit this corner of the Caribbean. Read on for my favorite vacation rentals in the Riviera Maya, from city escapes in Cancún to beachy stays in Tulum and everything in between.

We've selected these listings based on Superhost and Guest Favorite status, ratings, amenities, location, decor, editor stays, and previous guest reviews.

Number of guests: 2Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Outdoor pool, Surrealist architecture, hammam, private hot tub

A true wellness escape, this one-bedroom loft inside the Babel Tulum community is perfect for travelers seeking a jungle refuge in one of Mexico’s most popular beach towns. The architecture alone is worth a stay: The community is an interpretation of the fantastical city and empire of Babylon, and this loft is one of many built around the communal outdoor pool and hammam. Inside, architectural details like chukum lime-finished walkways and a private hot tub on the terrace make this a cozy, romantic stay for two.

Location: TulumThings to do nearby: Sian Ka’an Biosphere Reserve, Tulum Beach Road, Gran Cenote

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 2 bedrooms, 2.5 bathsWhy we love it: Outdoor pool, oceanfront location, priority access to Tulum beach clubs

Surrounded by jungle on one side and beachfront on the other, this two-bedroom will enmesh you in nature—plus, it’s just steps away from some of the Riviera Maya’s best snorkeling. Located on the ground floor and in a tranquil gated community, this is indoor-outdoor living at its finest, with a swim-up pool that looks directly out to the Caribbean Sea. For travelers seeking a relaxing stay, this spot on a secluded bay feels worlds away from bustling Tulum Town.

Location: TulumThings to do nearby: Casa Cenote, Tulum Beach Road, Mesoamerican Barrier Reef System

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Lush grounds, cenote access, bikes for rent, private terrace

This tree house suite near Cenote Dos Ojos is perfect for families or friends eager to travel together and explore Riviera Maya’s wild nature. Located in Parque Dos Ojos, a family-run lodge, the tree house features one bedroom with two queen beds, a kitchenette, and a seating area that opens to an expansive private terrace with a hammock. The property includes an open-air observation tower, perfect for spotting toucans and flycatchers at sunrise, and offers close access to Sistema Sac Actun, the longest underwater cave system in the world.

Location: TulumThings to do nearby: Cenote Dos Ojos, Puerto Aventuras, Playa del Carmen

Number of guests: 12Bed and bath: 4 bedrooms, 4 bathsWhy we love it: Rooftop pool, open-concept living area, Brutalist design, location inside a national reserve

This striking Brutalist villa sits in the heart of the Sian Ka’an Biosphere Reserve. It’s built with sustainability-minded principles in order to keep the surrounding jungle a haven for wildlife. The four-bedroom home (three king bedrooms and a room with two twins) was designed by the Mexico City–based architecture firm Productora and features open-concept living spaces, plus a spiral staircase that leads to a rooftop with a pool, outdoor seating, and expansive views of the jungle and the Caribbean Sea. You’ll have to draw straws for the primary bedroom: It features two private patios as well as its own hot tub and en suite bathroom.

Location: Sian Ka’an Biosphere ReserveThings to do nearby: Tulum Beach Road, Sian Ka’an Biosphere Reserve, Boca Paila Lagoon

Number of guests: 2Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Rooftop pool, easy access to ferry, walkable to cafés and restaurants

Conveniently located near the ferry to Isla Mujeres, this studio is ideal for couples or solo travelers eager for a quick getaway to Cancún. The studio has a king-size bed, a sofa, a fully equipped kitchen, and a balcony perfect for enjoying quiet mornings, as well as access to a rooftop dipping pool with views of Cancún and the surrounding jungle. The property is only a 10-minute walk from the area’s bustling markets, cafés, and restaurants.

Location: CancúnThings to do nearby: Isla Mujeres, downtown Cancún, Playa Puerto Juárez

Number of guests: 6Bed and bath: 2 bedrooms, 2 bathsWhy we love it: Resort-style amenities, walking distance from restaurants and cafés, laundry

This contemporary condo within the private residential community of Suutuk in Playa del Carmen is perfect for groups seeking equal parts wellness and adventure. Featuring two bedrooms (a queen and a double) and a sofa bed, the home comfortably sleeps six and is just a short drive away from the Caribbean Sea. During your stay, guests have access to the building’s resort-style amenities, including a rooftop pool and grill, lounge spaces, a gym, and a sauna.

Location: Playa del CarmenThings to do nearby: Quinta Avenida, Xcaret Park, Cenote Chaak Tun

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 2 bathsWhy we love it: Private plunge pool, ocean views, walkable location

Just a short walk from Playa del Carmen’s bustling Quinta Avenida, this two-story loft is ideal for travelers who want to be in the heart of the town’s restaurant and nightlife scene. The home features one bedroom with a king-size bed and a sofa bed in the living room, plus a fully equipped kitchen, seating area, and private plunge pool. Guests also have access to a shared rooftop replete with an outdoor pool, hot tub, firepit, and views of the Caribbean Sea.

Location: Playa del CarmenThings to do nearby: Quinta Avenida, Playa Coco, Cozumel Island

Number of guests: 12Bed and bath: 3 bedrooms, 3.5 bathroomsWhy we love it: Private pool, cenote access, group-friendly, gated community

Set in a gated community in the jungle, this three-bedroom comfortably accommodates up to 12 guests, making it ideal for families and groups. The space includes a fully equipped kitchen and an outdoor lounge area with a dipping pool, seating, and a barbecue grill, making it the perfect home for entertaining and dining alfresco. For adventures off the property, a private cenote and the white sand of Playa Xcalacoco are only a short drive away.

Location: Playa del CarmenThings to do nearby: Playa Xcalacoco, Punta Esmeralda, Quinta Avenida

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1.5 bathsWhy we love it: Secluded location, private plunge pool, cenote access, elevated architecture

This home offers intimate access to the Tulum jungle, a tranquil paradise that feels a world away from bustling downtown Tulum, about a 20-minute drive away, and Playa del Carmen, a 40-minute drive away. Built on stilts to limit environmental impact, this home features an open-concept layout with a double bed and sofa bed, an expansive living area, a fully equipped kitchen, and a plunge pool. But perhaps the retreat’s finest feature is outdoors—steps from the home is a private cenote, replete with sparkling turquoise water.

Location: San PabloThings to do nearby: Cenote Dos Ojos, Xel-Há Park, Tulum Archaeological Zone

Number of guests: 2Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Private rooftop plunge pool, beachfront access, sauna

On the serene shores of Soliman Bay, this one-bedroom penthouse is perfect for couples seeking a peaceful, romantic escape on the Caribbean coast. The condo features a cozy king-size bedroom and a fully equipped kitchen and living area—but the real jewel of this property is its stunning private rooftop pool and terrace overlooking the sparkling turquoise bay below. Guests can also enjoy access to the bay’s secluded white-sand beach, plus building amenities like an oceanfront swimming pool, gym, and sauna.

Location: Tankah CuatroThings to do nearby: Tulum Beach Road, Akumal Bay, Casa Cenote

Number of guests: 4Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Private pool, pickleball court, open-concept kitchen, lush vegetation

Wake up to birds chirping at this idyllic home in Akumal: an A-frame suite perfect for two. Surrounded by lush tropical vegetation and set within a gated community, a stay here is all about being outdoors. The upstairs loft features a cozy king-size bed, while the ground floor offers an open-concept kitchen and coffee bar that opens to a private pool often visited by butterflies. Guests can use the on-site community pickleball court or take a short drive to Xpu-Ha, a turquoise beach just five minutes away.

Location: AkumalThings to do nearby: Xpu-Ha, Puerto Aventuras, Playa del Carmen
